reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies between reliability and resolution: recalibration techniques such as Temperature scaling, Platt MAP, and EB τ adjust forecast confidence to align with empirical frequencies, thereby improving reliability (e.g., reducing Brier score and ECE), but do not enhance the discriminative capacity of models. Resolution is a measure of how well forecasts separate outcomes, and low resolution implies that even highly confident predictions fail to distinguish winners from losers. This is captured by the Murphy resolution metric, which is near zero in the current setup. The floor stress test (`runSyntheticFloorStressBakeoff`) simulates live diagnostic conditions to evaluate whether recalibration can lift performance above established thresholds (PROVEN floors). When no method passes these floors, it indicates that resolution—rather than reliability—is the limiting factor. Thus, the system must ensure that engine resolution is sufficient before enabling calibration adjustments. Failure to do so leads to a false sense of accuracy without true predictive utility.
